primitives.note: Love Tap adds bonus physical damage to the first attack (basic attack or Double Up) against an unmarked target; against a single dummy it can only trigger once, on the opening hit.
Love Tap's bonus damage is conditional on the target being unmarked; since the dummy is the only target, the mark never resets after the first proc.
Double Up's primary hit and Make It Rain's cast are fixed-formula damage delivered on cast/cast-delay.
Double Up's bounce requires a second enemy positioned behind the target; a 1-target dummy fight has no secondary target, so the bounce (and its reduced-crit damage) never occurs.

Double Up's bounce crits at a reduced (50% bonus crit damage) rate and always crits if it kills the primary target; each Bullet Time wave independently crits at a reduced (30% bonus crit damage) rate.
Make It Rain deals magic damage in 8 ticks (every 0.25s) over its 2s duration.
Strut's active grants a flat 4s bonus attack speed buff, useful for both autos and Double Up casts.
Landing Love Tap's mark on a new target cuts Strut's current cooldown by ~2s (ability-haste-affected, exact multiplier unresolved in the bin).
Bullet Time is an up-to-3s channel that blocks other actions (attacking, casting, moving) and can be cancelled in its final ~0.1s at no loss of effect.
Bullet Time fires 14-18 separately-timed waves over the channel, each a distinct damage instance able to crit on its own.
Double Up's cast time is defined as the Basic Attack Timer, so it occupies an auto-attack's timing slot and is sped up by attack speed.
Mana costs (40/45/80/100) constrain how many casts of each ability fit inside the 15s window.

needsBespoke.why: All damage-relevant behavior (once-only marked-target bonus, positional bounce that a dummy fight nullifies, a ticking DoT, a channelled multi-wave crit-capable ultimate, a cast tied to the attack timer, and a cooldown refund) maps onto existing primitives; no unique state machine beyond them is required.

unsettled.question: Since Double Up's cast time is defined as 'Basic Attack Timer' rather than a fixed cast time, does casting Q replace/consume a normal auto-attack in the rotation (i.e., you cannot both auto-attack and cast Q at the same moment), and does attack speed shorten Q's effective cast time the same way it shortens an auto's windup?
options: Q occupies the same timing slot as a basic attack: casting Q instead of attacking, and attack speed buffs speed up how often Q can be fired

proposal: Assume max ranks (R at rank 3) and a full item build; the dummy starts unmarked.
Land the first hit (basic attack or Double Up) to trigger Love Tap's one-time bonus damage against the dummy.
Cast Strut (W) early for its attack-speed active, speeding up subsequent autos and Double Up casts.
Cast Bullet Time (R) as soon as it is available, since the dummy cannot interrupt the up-to-3s channel and it deals the largest chunk of physical damage.
Between R's availability, cast Double Up (Q) on cooldown, weaving in normal basic attacks, and cast Make It Rain (E) on cooldown for its magic DoT.
Recast Strut (W) whenever its cooldown comes back up (aided by any Love Tap cooldown refunds) to keep the attack-speed buff active as much as possible.
Continue alternating Q casts/autos and E casts on cooldown, respecting mana costs, for the remainder of the 15s fight.
questions: Should the opener lead with Bullet Time immediately (locking MF into an uninterruptible channel for up to 3s) or build up attack speed/Love Tap value first before committing to R?
Is there an assumed mana pool/regen sufficient to sustain a full Q/W/E rotation for 15s, or does mana genuinely gate how often each ability is cast?
Does Double Up's attack-timer-based cast time mean it should be modeled as replacing an auto-attack slot in the rotation rather than as an independent cast on its own cooldown?
At what level/item state (crit chance, attack speed, AD/AP mix) should this rotation be evaluated, since it changes how much value Strut's active and Q/R crits contribute?
